articles.title: Hawthorn stun Fremantle and record Perth crowd with qualifying final win
articles.summary: Minor premiers suffer first home defeat of the season. Hawks never let up after first half onslaught. Sign up for our free weekly AFL newsletter. Nick Watson produced his usual bag of wizardry tricks and James Sicily led a rock-solid defence as Hawthorn ended Fremantle’s perfect home record in…
body: The Hawks kicked six goals to one in a dominant first half in Thursday night’s clash to set up the 10.12 (72) to 5.10 (40) win and secure a home preliminary final.
Fremantle, who had been a perfect 12-0 at Optus Stadium this season, will now confront either Carlton or Geelong in a cut-throat semi-final in Perth next week.
The Dockers were a dominant force during the home-and-away season, stringing together a 14-game winning streak at one stage on the way to a league-best 19-4 record.
But the minor premiers looked overawed in the finals cauldron on Thursday night in front of 59,446 fans – Fremantle’s largest ever home crowd.

articles.title: Sarr needs time to process collapse of Liverpool move
articles.summary: Crystal Palace forward Ismaila Sarr will need time to process the collapse of his proposed move to Liverpool, says Eagles head coach Pierre Sage.
body: The Senegal attacker, who was the club's top scorer last season, was linked with a move to Anfield late in the transfer window, but ended up staying at Selhurst Park.
Sage admitted: "He has to digest for sure because it's a dream for a lot of players to play with this kind of club ( Liverpool ).
"He had a good opportunity but in the end it didn't work. If he wants to continue, you have to have a good season with us as he did last year. We know he needs time.
"Like every bad situation, time does the job and we need time for that."

articles.title: How do European squad lists work?
articles.summary: Our Ask Me Anything team explain the rules that teams have to stick to when selecting their Champions League, Europa League and Conference League squads.
body: The Premier League transfer window has only just closed, but some teams immediately had another deadline to meet - registering their Champions League, Europa League or Conference League squads.
Clubs had to submit their senior team players to Uefa by 22:59 BST on Wednesday.
But squads are actually split into two separate lists - and there are a number of criteria that have to be met.
List A contains a maximum of 25 players, with a minimum of eight 'locally trained' squad members. Of those eight, no more than four can be 'association-trained' instead of 'club-trained'.

articles.title: The Athletic’s Findings From Dianna Russini-Mike Vrabel Affair Investigation Are a Nothing Burger That’ll Disappoint NFL Fans
articles.summary: On Thursday, The Athletic released its findings from the investigation into Dianna Russini’s unprofessional relationship with New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel, and it is more about covering the outlet’s butt when it comes to the news she covered for them instead of delving into whether…
body: One of the biggest stories in the NFL this spring actually came off the field and had nothing to do with one of the league’s athletes. Instead, fans were captivated by an apparent affair that was happening between the popular insider and veteran coach.

Photos of the pair, who are both married, emerged showing what looked to be an intimate moment while vacationing together at an adults-only resort in Arizona. It led to a boatload of follow-up stories that seemed to show the two had an ongoing relationship for quite some time. While Russini denied that whatever was going on with Vrabel affected her work for The Athletic, she was eventually suspended and then stepped down from her role with the news outlet. The Patriots coach also had to own up to the obvious affair and take time away from the team to try to fix his marriage.

articles.title: Hamilton reveals hope of becoming first black Ferrari driver to win in Italy
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton says he has been considering the magnitude of potentially becoming the first black Ferrari Formula 1 driver to win a home race for the team, ahead of this weekend's Italian Grand Prix.
body: The seven-time world champion has enjoyed a much improved second campaign in red, with a maiden Grand Prix victory for the team in Barcelona in June helping to keep him in title contention, as he trails Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli by 59 points with 11 rounds remaining.
Hamilton's hopes of claiming victory in Monza have been boosted by the fact Antonelli will start from the back of the grid as he serves a penalty for exceeding his engine-part allowance.

Asked what a prospective 107th career Grand Prix win would mean to him, Hamilton said: "I've really thought coming into this weekend, as I pondered, just thinking of the sheer magnitude of the concept that I'm coming to this Grand Prix, I didn't even know that I had I was equal with Michael [Schumacher] on [five Monza] wins, for example.
"But the thought that there's a first ahead of me, in the sense that potentially, if I was to win, you go into new territory.

articles.title: Barcelona already working on renewing three teenage breakout stars – report
articles.summary: FC Barcelona closed the summer transfer window on Tuesday with several new signings while also bidding goodbye to a number of players from the senior team as well as the youth setup.
body: With the window now closed, sporting director Deco now has a clear picture of the club’s Financial Fair Play situation.
Now, the sporting department can turn its attention to another priority: securing the futures of several key young players.
Barcelona deliberately avoided opening renewal negotiations while the market was open, with the focus being on completing their transfer operations. That changes now.
Indeed, according to MARCA, the Catalans’ immediate priority is to renew the contracts of three teenage starlets: Marc Bernal, Hamza Abdelkarim and Xavi Espart.

articles.title: Golfer born with no hands relishes Pro-Am experience
articles.summary: A Jersey teenager born with a congenital limb deficiency has described taking part in the British Masters Pro-Am golf tournament as the "best trip" of his life. Adam Dalton, who lives by the motto 'no hands, no limits', has underdeveloped arms, no hands and only the use of his left leg.
body: On 26 August the 21-year-old took part in the celebrity event at the Belfry, Sutton Coldfield, which acts as a curtain-raiser for the four-day British Masters.
Dalton was teamed with professional golfers Hennie du Plessis and Marcus Armitage and finished in third place overall. He said the pair "were so lovely and really intrigued with my game".
Dalton first discovered golf while trying out many sports to see which he could enjoy playing without pain.
He found that it did not cause discomfort for his prosthetic leg, and has since the age of 16 been a member at the Royal Jersey Golf Club.

articles.title: Mal Benning to be honoured, Choudhury winning Sheffield United debut
articles.summary: Welcome to Dev's Digest, the agenda-setting Sky Sports column where Dev Trehan delivers exclusive news and reflects some of the key developments for British South Asians in Football.
body: Mal Benning will be recognised with the football pioneer accolade at this month's Asian Football Awards, Sky Sports News can exclusively reveal.
Last season - on Valentine's Day - Benning made the 500th professional appearance of his career, a feat very few British South Asians have achieved in English football.
Benning broke through as a teenager under Dean Smith at Walsall during the 2012/13 season and had a loan spell at York City before joining Mansfield Town in 2015.

'Sir Mal' - as he was affectionately known by the Stags faithful - went on to earn legendary status, scoring against Mansfield's bitter rivals Chesterfield in April 2018 as he made over 250 appearances before joining Port Vale in the summer of 2021.
